project.name: group-grub
project.one_liner: Slack-native agentic group food ordering: an admin opens a budgeted DoorDash group order, per-person AI agents negotiate each participant's sub-order in Slack DMs, then a Rain-minted card pays (and is intentionally declined, with proof) through the DoorDash Drive sandbox.

hackathon.notes_for_judging: Rain cards are dummy cards; orders will be DECLINED by design. Capturing and displaying proof of the attempted-then-declined transaction is a FEATURE (decline-proof page). DoorDash API is sandbox-only; no real orders occur.

project.full_context: An admin runs `/begin-order` in Slack with: a list of users, a total budget, and a restaurant (e.g. McDonald's, Burger King, Applebee's — agent uses best judgment to resolve what the admin meant). The bot posts an 'announcement menu' message in an admin-specified channel saying a group order has been announced. Each listed participant receives a Slack DM from a dedicated AI agent (one agent pod per person, running the goose docker image on Kubernetes, backed by OpenRouter model z-ai/glm-5.2). Each participant gets a fair share of the total budget. The agent lists orderable items from the chosen restaurant, takes free-form conversation, offers suggestions, adds items to the participant's cart, and always enforces the sub-budget — suggesting removals when over. When the agent has a candidate order it asks the user to confirm (yes → submitted; no → keep iterating). A confirmed user may still reopen and change their order until the group order closes. Each confirmation updates the channel announcement message ('X has confirmed'). The group order closes when ALL users confirm OR when the admin-configured timer expires — whichever, there is then ALWAYS a 2-minute grace period during which users may still modify orders. After grace: mint a Rain card for the order total, then submit the order through the DoorDash Drive sandbox using that card. The card is a dummy; the payment attempt will decline — record and surface the decline proof. A web frontend (Vite + React + Node) has: (1) an admin panel behind basic HTTP auth (username `carson`, password `1234`) where the admin enters Rain client rules for card creation, sets the delivery address, and manages which Slack users are admins / may create orders; (2) a past-orders page; (3) a live current-order page fed over a websocket showing who is ordering what in real time. The Go orchestrator server exposes HTTP for the web server and the websocket for live order content. Hard security rule: NO order may ever exceed $300 total. Menu data: FIRST attempt browser-use in Stealth Mode to scrape live DoorDash menus for a SPECIFIC restaurant location; if that fails or is unreliable, FALL BACK to the local Kaggle CSV dataset (restaurantmenuchanges.csv) loaded into Postgres.

tech_stack.backend: Go — orchestrator: Slack events/commands, order state machine, budget math, Rain card minting, DoorDash Drive sandbox submission, HTTP API + websocket for frontend, Postgres persistence
tech_stack.agents: One agent per participant. Docker base image: ghcr.io/aaif-goose/goose:sha-86eec2a. LLM: OpenRouter model id z-ai/glm-5.2. Agents run as Kubernetes Jobs/Pods (DigitalOcean cluster, 3 nodes allowed). Agents talk to the orchestrator over HTTP for menu/cart/budget tools and DM users via Slack.
tech_stack.frontend: Vite + Node + React, deployed on Railway. Basic HTTP auth carson/1234 for admin panel.
tech_stack.data: Postgres on Railway. Kaggle dataset restaurantmenuchanges.csv (5007 rows; columns: createdOn, changeOperation, market, city, menuItemName, menuItemDescription, menuItemCurrentPrice, menuItemPreviousPrice, menuItemImageUrl, menuItemCategory, menuItemAverageRating, menuItemRatingCount, restaurantName, restaurantDescription, restaurantAddress, restaurantImageUrl, restaurantPriceRange, restaurantLatitude, restaurantLongitude).

hard_rules: NO order total may ever exceed $300 — enforce server-side in the Go orchestrator, not just UI.
Always apply the 2-minute grace period after all-confirmed OR timer expiry, before minting the card.
Admin panel basic auth is exactly username `carson`, password `1234`.
Rain cards are dummy cards: the DoorDash payment WILL decline. Persist the decline evidence (request, response, timestamps, card id) and expose it in the UI as the decline-proof feature.

This codebase is written by and for an AI agent (Ralph loop): keep comments minimal and only where they inform the NEXT loop iteration. Do NOT write an exhaustive test suite — only test logic that must survive repeated runs (state machine, budget split, $300 cap, timer/grace transitions, JWT signing).
Never commit API_KEYS, docker-config, or k8s* files (already git-ignored).
architecture_decisions: Orchestrator owns ALL state (Postgres). Agents are stateless tools-over-HTTP clients; killing an agent pod must never lose an order.

Agent <-> orchestrator contract: GET /internal/menu?restaurant=..., GET/POST /internal/orders/{id}/participants/{uid}/cart, POST .../confirm, GET .../budget. Agents receive ORDER_ID, PARTICIPANT_SLACK_ID, ORCHESTRATOR_URL, SLACK creds, OPEN_ROUTER_KEY via k8s env.
Budget split: fair share = floor(total_cents / n_participants); remainder stays unallocated as buffer.

Order state machine: OPEN -> COLLECTING -> GRACE(2m) -> MINTING -> SUBMITTING -> DECLINED_PROOF_CAPTURED -> CLOSED (plus CANCELLED). Announcement message re-rendered on every participant confirm/unconfirm and state change.
Websocket broadcasts participant cart/confirm events keyed by order id for the live current-order page.
